checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md, SLOGAN.txt, VERIFICATION.md, and verification.py (read only)
correctness.rationale: The frozen decimal expansion of η* was incorrect at the printed precision (the supplied checker substituted a machine float into the gain formula). The exact definition and all preferences survive. The repair corrects the expansion in RESULT.md and SLOGAN.txt, and supplies exact rational bounds in verification.py and VERIFICATION.md. Independently integrating the bridge kernel gives the stated squared-covariance gains and baseline 1/30. The position derivative changes sign once until its stationary branch reaches 1 at η=11/336, with t=1 uniquely optimal at equality. The velocity stationary condition has a strictly increasing noise map on the interval from the noiseless optimum to √6−2. The optimized log-gain ratio has strictly negative derivative, including across the position endpoint stage by the unique-optimizer envelope identity: Vp≤1/12<6/25<Vv at the velocity optimum. Exact comparisons at 11/336 and 1/25 give opposite signs; velocity stationarity and gain equality give (Jp(1)−Jv)Vv′=(Vp(1)−Vv)Jv′. This gives the stated polynomial, with opposite endpoint signs and all seven derivative Bernstein coefficients in (−53,−52). Monotonicity of Jv,Vv on the narrow rational time enclosure bounds the gain-equality quotient and places η* strictly between 0.03486395077318212468 and 0.03486395077318212469. This certifies the corrected digits; independent replay uses no packaged code. The corrected final statement has exactly the two stated tie designs at η*, one elsewhere.
residual_risks: Numerical illustrations are not the proof of the all-noise classification.
Equal noise variance is for the specified unit-time calibrated readouts; changing that calibration changes the design problem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general gain formula can be adapted to a derivative readout, but it does not give the time extrema, their variance separation, or the sign of the optimized gain comparison. The integrated-bridge covariance on an ordered triangle is not a single product kernel.

evidence: The derivative-only record does cover the unique noise-monotone velocity timing for the same bridge and path risk, including its limiting interval.
The Wiener quadrature analogue gives a terminal-value/derivative tie near noise 0.1260852 but under a different target; the general Gaussian criterion computes the gain for any given design.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Velocity timing alone says nothing about whether a displacement sensor wins or when its optimum reaches the endpoint. Likewise a general gain objective is not a solution to the global comparison; the nonoverlapping optimal observation variances and exact displacement derivative supply additional information.

evidence: Lachal distinguishes integrating a Brownian bridge from making a bridge out of integrated Brownian motion.
The integrated-Wiener quadrature record has a dual-mode switch, but uses unpinned Brownian motion and scalar quadrature error, not path loss.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Replacing the path L² risk by the variance of a path integral changes the numerator from an integral of squares to a squared integral; conditioning on the pin also changes the kernel. The dual-mode results are not equivalent by name, unit change, or a relabeling of the observables.

originality.rationale: The final corrected claim is the joint two-mode decision and its two thresholds. Integrated-bridge covariances, the Gaussian design criterion, and even the same bridge's derivative-only time classification are not claimed as new. The closest joint-modality result concerns a different process and scalar loss. The correction to the numeric expansion does not create new priority.

Catalogue dates do not establish order among related findings.

value.rationale: With a resource limit of one observation, sensor choice and timing need not optimize the same feature of the prior. The exact terminal-placement stage and later jump to an interior velocity reading answer that joint decision for every positive noise level. The observation-variance separation explains why the crossover cannot recur and provides a reusable design argument, not just a fitted crossing number. Correcting the decimal leaves this contribution intact.
residual_risks: A mathematical benchmark for one calibrated reading and unweighted path risk, not an assertion about hardware or general mixed-noise designs.
